description: Programming microcontrollers close to the metal: GPIO, timers, interrupts, analog input, serial buses and a small real-time scheduler, with power budgets that matter for solar-powered field devices. Taught to the depth of a leading introductory embedded systems course.
modelledOn: Lee and Seshia, Introduction to Embedded Systems: A Cyber-Physical Systems Approach
Valvano, Embedded Systems: Introduction to ARM Cortex-M Microcontrollers
outcomes: Read a microcontroller datasheet and reference manual and configure peripherals through memory-mapped registers.
Write bare-metal C for GPIO, timers, PWM, interrupts and ADC on an ARM Cortex-M or AVR board.
Design interrupt-driven and polled drivers and reason about latency and shared-data hazards.
Communicate with sensors and other devices over UART, I2C and SPI and decode the traffic on a logic analyser.
Implement a cooperative scheduler and a simple pre-emptive RTOS task set and analyse schedulability.
Estimate and reduce energy consumption with sleep modes, clock gating and duty cycling.

units.title: Embedded systems and microcontroller architecture
topics: What makes a system embedded: constraints on cost, power, size, timing and reliability
Microcontroller anatomy: core, flash, SRAM, peripherals, buses, clock tree, reset
ARM Cortex-M and AVR compared; the memory map and memory-mapped registers
Toolchain: cross-compiler, linker script, startup code, flashing, debugging with a probe; simulators
Reading a datasheet and reference manual; writing the first blink in bare-metal C

units.title: GPIO, timers and PWM
topics: GPIO configuration: modes, pull-ups, drive strength, speed; reading buttons and debouncing
Driving LEDs, relays, seven-segment displays, keypads, character LCDs
Timer peripherals: prescalers, counters, compare and capture, overflow
Measuring time, generating delays and periodic events without blocking
PWM for LED dimming, servo control and DC motor speed with an H-bridge

units.title: Interrupts
topics: Interrupt controller (NVIC), vector table, priorities, nesting, latency
Writing interrupt service routines; volatile, atomicity and critical sections
External interrupts, timer interrupts, software interrupts
Foreground-background design; deferring work from an ISR
Watchdog timers and fault handlers

units.title: ADC, DAC and sensors
topics: ADC principles: resolution, sampling rate, reference voltage, quantisation; successive approximation
Reading analog sensors: temperature, light, soil moisture, potentiometers; voltage dividers and conditioning
Oversampling, filtering and calibration in software
DAC and PWM-based analog output; driving a speaker
Digital sensors with pulse outputs: ultrasonic distance, DHT humidity

units.title: Serial communication: UART, I2C, SPI
topics: UART: framing, baud rate, parity; printf over serial; a command-line interface
I2C: addressing, start/stop, ACK, clock stretching; reading an accelerometer or RTC
SPI: modes, chip select, full duplex; driving a display or SD card
Decoding each bus with a logic analyser; common wiring faults
Other links: CAN, USB and wireless modules (Bluetooth, LoRa, GSM) in brief

units.title: Real-time scheduling basics
topics: Timing requirements: hard and soft real time, deadlines, jitter
Super-loop and cooperative schedulers; state machines for concurrent behaviour
Pre-emptive multitasking: tasks, context switch, stacks; a tiny RTOS (FreeRTOS)
Rate-monotonic and earliest-deadline-first scheduling; utilisation bounds; priority inversion and inheritance
Inter-task communication: queues, semaphores, mutexes

units.title: Low-power design
topics: Where energy goes: active, sleep, peripherals, radios; measuring current
Sleep modes, wake-up sources, clock scaling, peripheral gating
Duty cycling and event-driven design; battery and solar budgeting for a field sensor
Energy-aware firmware design for devices in rural Ghana

units.title: Embedded software engineering and project
topics: Driver layering, hardware abstraction, configuration, code organisation
Testing embedded code: unit tests on the host, hardware-in-the-loop, logging
Robustness: brown-out, EMI, input validation, firmware update
Project: a complete device such as a weather station, irrigation controller or prepaid meter prototype

schedule.title: What makes a system embedded
schedule.exercise: Short comparison: choose a microcontroller for a prepaid electricity meter from three datasheets and justify the choice on cost, power, memory and peripherals.

tasks.title: Identify the core, flash, SRAM and peripheral blocks of an AVR microcontroller on the hardware bench and note each block's size
Read and write memory-mapped port registers for an AVR and an ARM Cortex-M board and compare their memory maps and register widths
Choose a platform for a solar-powered field sensor from three options, weighing cost, power and reliability evidence, and justify it on a rubric

schedule.title: Toolchain, datasheets and first blink
schedule.exercise: Write a short note tracing a C program from source to flashed binary, and annotate which datasheet table you used to find the LED port register.

tasks.title: Wire an LED and resistor to a microcontroller pin on the bench, write a bare-metal blink in C and watch it toggle at one hertz
Compile a blink program with a cross compiler, inspect the linker map to find where code and variables sit, and explain the startup code
Find the register and bit needed for a new pin in a datasheet, then fix a faulty blink program that has a wrong data direction setting

schedule.title: GPIO and timers
schedule.exercise: Design a debounce routine for a keypad and explain how a timer prescaler gives a 1 ms tick.

tasks.title: Wire a push button with a pull-up resistor, read it in C and count presses, then observe the bounces on the logic analyser
Drive a four-digit seven-segment display by multiplexing and show a counter from 0000 to 9999 without visible flicker
Configure a hardware timer with a prescaler and compare register to generate an exact 100 Hz tick and verify it on a scope

schedule.title: Time and PWM
schedule.exercise: Calculate PWM duty cycles for a servo and a DC motor and write a short note on why delay loops are unsuitable in real products.

tasks.title: Blink two LEDs at different rates using a timer tick instead of a blocking delay and show both keep their timing
Control a hobby servo from 0 to 180 degrees with PWM using a pulse width of 1 to 2 ms and check the pulse on the scope
Drive a DC motor with an H-bridge, ramp its speed with PWM, add a direction button and protect against shoot-through

schedule.title: Interrupts and robust firmware
schedule.exercise: Write a short note on why a variable shared with an ISR must be volatile and how you protect a multi-byte counter.

tasks.title: Toggle an LED from an external interrupt on a button press and compare the response with a polling loop
Count pulses in an ISR and print them from the main loop using volatile variables and a safe copy that avoids torn reads
Debug a firmware with a race condition and a missed watchdog kick, then redesign it to defer work from the ISR and add a watchdog

schedule.title: ADC and analog sensors
schedule.exercise: Compute ADC resolution and quantisation error for a 10-bit converter at 5 V and design a divider for a thermistor.

tasks.title: Read a potentiometer with the ADC, print raw counts and volts, and check the quantisation step against the datasheet resolution
Read a soil moisture sensor and a temperature sensor, calibrate each against two reference points and display the converted values
Reduce noise on a light sensor reading using 16x oversampling and a moving average, and measure the improvement in standard deviation

schedule.title: DAC, speaker and pulse sensors
schedule.exercise: Short exercise: calculate the time-of-flight distance for an ultrasonic echo and explain the DHT sensor's timing protocol.

tasks.title: Play a 440 Hz tone on a speaker using PWM and a low-pass filter, and verify the frequency on the scope
Measure distance with an ultrasonic sensor by timing the echo pulse, and display it with a median filter to reject outliers
Read temperature and humidity from a DHT sensor using bit-banged timing and handle checksum failures without blocking the main loop

schedule.title: UART, I2C and SPI
schedule.exercise: Draw the timing diagram for one UART byte, one I2C write and one SPI transfer, and compare their wires and speeds.

tasks.title: Send printf output over UART at 9600 baud and decode one byte from the signal by measuring bit times on the logic analyser
Read acceleration from an I2C sensor and a time from an RTC, using the datasheet addresses, and print both to serial
Write a driver for an SPI display or SD card that handles mode and chip select, then troubleshoot a wrong clock polarity

schedule.title: Bus debugging and other links
schedule.exercise: Short reflection: choose between LoRa, GSM and Bluetooth for a remote tank level monitor, citing range, power and cost.

tasks.title: Capture an I2C transaction on the logic analyser and decode the address, read-write bit and acknowledge bits
Find three planted wiring faults (swapped lines, missing pull-up, wrong address) on an I2C and SPI board using the logic analyser
Select a wireless link for a remote water-level sensor, scoring range, power, cost and coverage evidence for LoRa, GSM and Bluetooth

schedule.title: Real-time basics and schedulers
schedule.exercise: Write a state machine design for a traffic light controller with a pedestrian button, and explain the timing needed.

tasks.title: Classify five systems as hard or soft real time, and measure jitter in a simulated periodic task on the visualiser
Implement a cooperative scheduler running three tasks at 10, 50 and 100 ms and check the timing with a toggled pin
Write a pre-emptive two-task round-robin kernel with separate stacks and a context switch, and explain the stack layout it uses

schedule.title: Real-time scheduling analysis
schedule.exercise: Problem set: test schedulability of three task sets with rate-monotonic and earliest-deadline-first analysis and explain a priority inversion.

tasks.title: Schedule three periodic tasks with rate-monotonic priorities on the visualiser and check each deadline is met for utilisation of 0.7
Connect a producer and consumer task with a queue and guard a shared resource with a mutex, and show no data is lost
Reproduce a priority inversion with three tasks and a mutex, then fix it with priority inheritance and show the high task meets its deadline

schedule.title: Low-power design
schedule.exercise: Compute battery life for a solar-and-battery field sensor from its duty cycle and per-state current draws, and propose two improvements.

tasks.title: Measure the current drawn by an AVR in active mode and sleep mode on the bench and compute the ratio
Put a sensor node to sleep and wake it from a timer and a button interrupt, then gate unused peripherals and record the saving
Design the duty cycle and battery and panel size for a sensor reporting every 10 minutes in Ghana, and verify the energy budget in simulation

schedule.title: Software engineering and project
schedule.exercise: Project plan: define requirements, driver layers, test plan and update strategy for a weather station or irrigation controller.

tasks.title: Split a monolithic sensor program into a hardware abstraction layer, driver and application files, and show the application compiles for two boards
Write host-side unit tests for a sensor-conversion and a ring-buffer module using mocks and run them on the PC before flashing
Build an irrigation controller prototype that reads soil moisture, drives a valve, logs events and recovers from brown-out, then test five faults
